chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

For the lost one (al-mafqud), the inheritors should withhold his wealth, striving to seek him in the land, for four years. So if they are not able to locate him, his wealth is distributed among the inheritors. And if he had children, the wealth is withheld, and spent upon his children for those four years.

key_terms.أَرْبَعَ سِنِينَ: Four years; the standard period for waiting for the lost one in Shia jurisprudence.
key_terms.الْمَفْقُودُ: The lost one; a person whose whereabouts are unknown but not confirmed dead.
key_terms.الْوَرَثَةُ: The inheritors; those entitled to the estate.
key_terms.وُلْدٌ: Children; offspring who may benefit from the withheld estate.

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling for the inheritance of a person with unknown whereabouts?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the four-year period (ajl) for determining the status of a missing person (al-mafqud), reflecting the juristic consensus on balancing the rights of heirs with the possibility of the person's return. It specifically highlights the provision for children, ensuring their maintenance is secured from the estate during the waiting period, a nuance that underscores the protective nature of Shia inheritance law regarding dependents.
